title: Introduce fleet-thermostat-autoscaler and microburst hedging for Dedicated capacity
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Recent incidents and internal perf runs showed oscillatory autoscaling behavior in Dedicated fleets when handling erratic request bursts. Binary scaling decisions coupled with short-timescale utilization signals caused throughput overshoot followed by sharp scale-downs, which produced transient latency spikes for tail-sensitive workloads. This PR introduces a "thermostat"-style autoscaler that smooths control actions across multiple timescales, preserves a small configurable headroom for microbursts, and provides explicit hedging credits to avoid oscillation-induced SLA violations.

Summary of changes: added a new autoscaler controller (fleet/thermostat_autoscaler) that computes a smoothed target capacity using an ensemble of windows (short/medium/long) and a conservative bias term, integrates with the reservation ledger to honor committed capacity, exposes a microburst-credit bank for ephemeral surges, and emits a compact telemetry surface to power alerting and chargeback. The controller is pluggable as a replacement autoscaler for Dedicated pools and defaults to a conservative mode behind a feature flag.

Key behaviors: 1) Multi-window smoothing: combine recent short-window Utilization, median medium-window, and 95th percentile long-window signals to derive a blended utilization estimate. 2) Thermostat bias: a tunable proportional bias (thermostat_delta) nudges target capacity up when long-window trends rise and down very slowly on declines to avoid rapid churn. 3) Microburst hedging: maintain a small warmlet of ephemeral capacity funded by a microburst_credit token bank; tokens replenish gradually and can be borrowed with safety backoff. 4) Safety fences: never scale below reservation commitments, clamp scale-down rates with a ramp-limit, and add a transient cooldown for pools that recently accepted hedged tokens. 5) Observability: emit util_blend, bias_contrib, hedged_tokens_used, cooldown_state, and decision_reason tags for every decision; add dashboards and an alert rule template. 6) Rollout plan: feature-flagged on Dedicated, gradual canary across low-traffic pools then wider rollout with automatic rollback on increased tail latencies.

Commits (high-level): - feat(autoscaler): initial thermostat_autoscaler controller and state machine - perf(telemetry): summary metrics and hdr sketch integration - api: microburst_credit ledger API and gRPC surface - safety: reservation and ramp-limit enforcement hooks - tests: unit + deterministic simulation harness for stochastic bursts - ci: perf benchmark job + flaky test fixes - docs: ops runbook and tuning guide

Files changed (high-level): - internal/fleet/autoscaler/thermostat_autoscaler.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/smoothing_windows.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/hedge_bank.go - internal/fleet/autoscaler/simulation/harness_test.go - internal/fleet/api/credits.proto - internal/fleet/controllers/scale_reconciler.go (integration points) - pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go - docs/ops/thermostat-autoscaler.md - test/integration/dedicated_autoscale_sim.py - .github/workflows/perf-bench.yml

Example config snippet: feature_gate: thermostatic_autoscaler: enabled; thermostat_delta: 0.12; short_window: 30s; medium_window: 5m; long_window: 30m; microburst_credit_capacity: 4pools; ramp_down_pct_per_min: 5%

Testing and validation: included a deterministic simulation harness with synthetic Poisson and heavy-tailed burst generators used to validate stability across 1k simulation runs and measure transient latency exposures. Added integration test that replays a 6-hour production traffic trace (sanitized) against a local Dedicated pool to ensure no regression in steady-state throughput. Perf benchmarks were added to CI (perf-bench job) to ensure controller decision latency stays <50ms at 5000 pools.

Review convo (summary): - Diego Ramos: "Can we prove that thermostat_delta won't systematically overshoot commitments?" Answer: used long-window percentile with conservative bias and clamp against reservation ledger; added unit test for a simulated uphill trend and refactored to add a 'bias_decay' param. - Morgan Lee: requested stronger invariants on token accounting to avoid double-spend during reconciles; fixed by moving credit transfer into single transactional reconciliation step and added idempotency keys. - Kai Nguyen: flagged potential e2e flakiness due to perf-bench variability; added HDR-sketch bucketing and deterministic seeding. - Security review (Priya Shah): minimal exposure (ledger API authenticated) but requested audit log entries for token borrow/repay flows; added audit events. Two rounds of small follow-ups and then approvals from Diego and Morgan.

CI summary: initial test run (2026-02-16) showed failing integration tests due to a race in the hedging bank; fixed in commit 3 and re-ran. Final CI status: unit tests (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass), lint (pass). Overall ci_status: pass.

Backward compatibility and safety: controller is feature-flagged and off by default. It respects reservation commitments and default ramp limits are conservative. No breaking changes to public APIs; credits.proto adds a backward compatible optional service.

Release notes: "Introduce Thermostat Autoscaler for Dedicated fleets: smoother autoscaling with microburst hedging, improved observability, and ops tuning guide. Feature-gated; opt-in rollout."

Follow-ups: - ENG-3124: auto-tune bias_decay using historical traces (tracked) - ENG-3187: add scheduler integration for locality-aware hedging - ENG-3301: expose per-tenant hedged-token billing metrics
release_notes: Introduce Thermostat Autoscaler: smoother Dedicated autoscaling with microburst credit hedging and observability; feature-flagged and opt-in; see ops runbook for tuning
